audit.whatIsWrong: Level 1, Levels 4-5, Level 6 and 2+ items were all scored Lucian or Skill against what the same rows' whys say: 'you both have weak level 1s', 'he E-in, W-stuns, and dumps a combo', 'this window is his unless his fury is empty', 'you out-scale no one'.
audit.why: 50% win rate, and the packet chart reads Skill, Lucian, Lucian, Renekton, Renekton, Skill, Skill — identical to the prose.
audit.corrected: win[0]/phases[0].side -> Skill; win[3]/phases[3].side and win[4]/phases[4].side -> Renekton; win[6]/phases[6].side -> Skill.

audit.whatIsWrong: phases[3] and phases[4] used the generic Lucian boilerplate on the two stages this page identifies as his.
audit.why: His spike is Fury, not a level: at 50+ Fury Ruthless Predator stuns for 1.5s instead of 0.75s, deals high damage and destroys damage shields. Slice and Dice's second charge is what closes the range.
audit.corrected: Both stages now state the Fury threshold and what it changes.

audit.whatIsWrong: Nothing anywhere mentioned that empowered Ruthless Predator destroys damage shields, or that it is an auto-attack reset.
audit.why: Shield destruction changes the all-in maths for any shield you or your support bring, and the auto reset means the burst lands on the wind-up rather than on a visible cast — that is when you leave, not after.
audit.corrected: Both written in: dosFull[0] gets the reset tell and the 16s rank-1 cooldown, dosFull[2] the shield-shatter.

audit.why: The needs-antiheal rule fires on Cull the Meek's heal; report[8] already says to add anti-heal early into his sustain, and dontsFull[0] now ties the buy to a concrete behaviour.
The packet suspectName 'Use Ardent Blaze' is a false positive — Ardent Blaze is Lucian's real W name.

edits.before: Passive double-shots win level 1 outright — Q through the wave on his last-hits and weave doubletaps on every step-up.
edits.after: Both level 1s are weak — deny his Cull the Meek last-hits and set up level 2 rather than trading into a flat W.

edits.before: Keep the pressure rolling but track Ruthless Predator (Stun) — your lead is HP-bar bullying, not all-in math, until items arrive.
edits.after: At 50+ Fury Ruthless Predator stuns 1.5s and shatters shields — he dashes in, stuns, and dumps before your E returns.

edits.before: The Culling adds lane-clear and execute chip — use it through walls on recalls and low-HP escapes.
edits.after: The Culling is a damage spike, not a lane flip — his stun catches you mid-channel unless his Fury is empty.

edits.before: You fall off relative to top-lane scalers — convert the lead into towers and roams before the 3-item brawlers arrive.
edits.after: He falls off and you stay relevant, but you out-scale nobody — close it before his teamfight lockdown decides games.

edits.before: Fury-empowered stun — never trade into a full rage bar. Until it’s spent, every commit is a coin flip.
edits.after: Ruthless Predator is 16s at rank 1 and resets his auto — the wind-up is the tell, not the cast.

edits.before: Renekton whiffs Ruthless Predator (Stun) and the lane briefly belongs to you.
edits.after: Empowered W destroys shields and stuns 1.5s — never commit into 50+ Fury.

edits.before: That is Renekton’s whole plan in one window — decline politely and watch it retire.
edits.after: Cull the Meek heals him every swing — buy Grievous Wounds before you extend.

notes: The written analysis on this page was already accurate — Fury threshold, double E, hold E for the stun chain — and the only thing wrong was the level chart contradicting it on four of seven rows, including Level 6, where whys[4] says outright 'this window is his'. Fury generation is faster when Renekton is low, which is why the chip-him-down plan can hand him the stun that kills you; that nuance is in Riot's passive text and is reflected in the Level 6 line. Nothing asserted about tenacity or Cleanse against the 1.5s stun.
